findings.title: Application Is Marked Debuggable
findings.cwe_id: CWE-215: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
findings.description: The application has android:debuggable="true" enabled. Attackers can connect JDWP debuggers via ADB, dump memory, inspect encryption keys, bypass security controls, and execute arbitrary code in app context.
findings.evidence: android:debuggable="true" is declared in AndroidManifest.xml under <application>.
findings.remediation: Ensure android:debuggable="false" is set in production release builds. In build.gradle, verify that buildTypes { release { debuggable false } } is enforced.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP Traffic Permitted
findings.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
findings.description: The application allows unencrypted HTTP network communication. Traffic sent over plaintext HTTP can be intercepted, read, or modified by adversaries via Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.
findings.evidence: 2 unencrypted HTTP URLs discovered in code (e.g., http://127.0.0.1, http://127.0.0.1/signup)
findings.remediation: Enforce HTTPS for all network endpoints. Configure Android Network Security Configuration (res/xml/network_security_config.xml) with cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" and ensure TLS 1.2+ is required.

findings.title: Insecure file:// Local URL Schemes Detected
findings.cwe_id: CWE-749: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
findings.description: The application references local 'file://' URI schemes (2 occurrences). If passed to WebViews with allowFileAccess enabled, this can lead to arbitrary local file disclosure and Cross-App Scripting.
findings.evidence: Detected file:// scheme references in code: file:///android_asset/unsafe_content.html, file:///android_asset/unsafe_content.html
findings.remediation: Avoid using file:// schemes. Use content:// URIs with FileProvider or modern WebViewAssetLoader to restrict file system access securely.

findings.title: Client-Side Root Detection Binary Checks Detected
findings.description: The application inspects standard root binary paths (/sbin/su, /su/bin/su) to detect rooted devices. Standard file-existence checks are easily bypassed via Frida hooking or root-hiding modules.
findings.remediation: Supplement client-side file checks with hardware-backed Play Integrity API verification and anti-tampering controls.
